chunks: What the Shaykh—may Allah Most High support him—informed me of, from Abū Jaʿfar Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī, from Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan and Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from his father Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan, from Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā, from ʿAlī ibn Muḥammad, from a man, from Sulaymān ibn Ḥafṣ al-Marwazī, who said:

Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام said: “Ghusl is with one ṣāʿ of water, and wudu (ablution) is with one mudd of water. The ṣāʿ of the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم is five amdād. A mudd is the weight of two hundred and eighty dirhams, a dirham is the weight of six dānīqs, a dānīq is the weight of six grains, and one grain is the weight of two barley grains of average size—not from the small ones and not from the large ones.”

key_terms.أَمْدَادٍ: plural of mudd, used to define the ṣāʿ
key_terms.الْغُسْلُ: ghusl (ritual bath) required for major ritual impurity
key_terms.حَبَّتَيْ شَعِيرٍ: two barley grains used as the finest illustrative weight measure
key_terms.دَوَانِيقَ: subunits of the dirham in weight measurement
key_terms.دِرْهَمًا: a unit of weight used to quantify the mudd
key_terms.صَاعٍ: a standard measure of volume used here for ghusl water
key_terms.مُدٍّ: a smaller measure of volume used here for wudu water

ai.seo_question: How much water is prescribed for ghusl and wudu (ablution) in this hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith states the measured amount of water for ghusl and wudu (ablution), and then defines these measures through a chain of weight units. It reflects precision in ritual purity law and preserves the Prophetic standard attributed to the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم.
